test_title: SSC CGL 2021 Tier-I (Held On : 19 April 2022 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In a right-angled triangle, the lengths of the medians from the vertices of acute angles are 7 cm and 4sqrt 6 cm. What is the length of the hypotenuse of the triangle (in cm)?
solution:
**Given data:**

Length of medians = 7 cm and 4√6 cm.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/30114a2a0b4b788f47c15e7c5da94dfdcab5df97060f211983dddeb9dec13091.png] 

In Δ ABC, AE = BE and BD = DC

⇒ ED = 1over2 AC

Let BE = x and BD = y

⇒ BC = 2y

Applying Pythagora's theorem to the Δ BEC

BE² + BC² = EC²

Substituting the value, we get-

x² + (2y)² = (4√6)²

⇒ 96 = x2 + 4y2 - (Equation 1)

Applying Pythagora's theorem to the Δ ABD

AB2 + BD2 = AD2

Substituting the value, we get-

(2x)2 + y2 = 72

⇒ 49 = 4x2 + y2 - (Equation 2)

Adding Equation 1 and Equation 2, we get- 

⇒ 5x² + 5y² = 145

⇒ x2 + y2 = 29

In Δ BED, x2 + y2 = ED² 

⇒ ED = √29.

AC = 2ED = 2√29.

∴ **The length of the hypotenuse of the triangle is 2√29.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cfb223f18f06b7e490444707ced579af3dc366691afbb86f949a6be3fc487c2b.png] 

In right angled Δ ABC, if AD and CE are the medians then,

⇒ 4(AD² + CE²) = 5AC²

Now, AD = 7 cm and CE = 4√6

⇒ 4[(7)² + (4√6)²] = 5AC²

⇒ 4(49 + 96) = 5AC²

⇒ 5AC² = 580

⇒ AC = 2√29

∴ The length of the hypotenuse of the triangle is 2√29.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** ⇒ AD² + CE² = 5ED²
